answer: A reputation bond works like an orchard: each agent stakes tokens that vest slowly, like trees maturing, so a Sybil farmer must fund many separate stakes and wait. A single comet-fast identity that appears, spams, and vanishes earns nothing because its bond is still locked, while a sable-dark market of cheap fake accounts cannot harvest rewards faster than the vesting schedule allows. Forging one credible identity is cheap; forging a hundred mature ones is ruinously expensive.
